title: The flash-sale checkout that never hits 25% off
topic: A holiday discount the AI 'finished' in one sitting
blurb: Spec says $500+ gets 25% off. The AI's function is very sure it does. Big carts will disagree.
prompt: Spec: sum every item, take 25% off at $500+ or 10% off at $100+, return the total. An AI intern shipped this for the flash sale. Review it.

segments.label: L2
segments.text: subtotal = sum(prices[i] for i in range(len(prices) - 1))

conclusion: AI summary: Sums all prices and applies 10% off at $100+ or 25% off at $500+. Ready for the sale.

flaws.corrupted: subtotal = sum(prices[i] for i in range(len(prices) - 1))

diagnosis_choices.label: Off-by-one: `range(len(prices) - 1)` stops before the last index, silently dropping the last item.
Python's `sum()` cannot accept a generator expression.

fix_choices.label: Use `range(1, len(prices))` to include the last item.
Use `range(len(prices) + 1)` so the last index is included.

flaws.explanation: `range(n)` generates `0 .. n-1`. Subtracting 1 cuts off the final element of `prices` (and gives 0 for a single-item cart!).
flaws.why_tempting: People remember 'last index is `len - 1`' and forget that `range()` already excludes its stop value.
flaws.catch_rule: Test loops on a 1-element list: if `range(len(xs) - 1)` runs 0 times, it's off by one.
flaws.hint: What's `subtotal` when the cart is just `prices = [200]`?

practice.problem: For `xs = [10, 20, 30]`, which values does `xs[i]` hit when `i` runs through `range(len(xs) - 1)`?
practice.answer: Only `10` and `20`. The last item, `30`, never gets added.

flaws.original: if subtotal >= 500: discount = 0.25  # check the higher threshold first

diagnosis_choices.label: Unreachable branch: any `subtotal >= 500` already matched `if subtotal >= 100` on L3.
`elif` cannot compare the same variable twice in Python.
`>= 500` should be `> 500` because $500 orders only get 10%.

fix_choices.label: Check the stricter condition first: `if subtotal >= 500:` (0.25), then `elif subtotal >= 100:` (0.10).
Remove the `else` branch so Python evaluates both `if` and `elif`.

flaws.explanation: In an `if / elif` chain, only the first true branch runs. Because every number `>= 500` is also `>= 100`, the 25% tier is dead code.
flaws.why_tempting: Listing tiers from smallest ($100) to largest ($500) reads naturally in English, even though `if/elif` requires the reverse.
flaws.catch_rule: In threshold `if/elif` chains, always order conditions from most restrictive to least restrictive (highest to lowest for `>=`).
flaws.hint: Walk a $600 order through lines 3–6. Which branch actually runs?

practice.problem: In `if score >= 60: g='D' elif score >= 90: g='A'`, what grade does 95 get?

clean_conclusion: Every item is summed, and a $500+ cart actually gets the 25% tier.

diagnosis: checkout_total should receive one scalar rather than a list of prices.
The function needs a separate argument for every price.
The callable should take the discount instead of the prices.
fix: Change prices to a single price argument.
Require separate price1 and price2 arguments.

diagnosis: The threshold should be applied to the first price only.
Subtotals below 100 qualify for this branch.
A 10% discount should be stored as 10.
The discount variable should contain the fraction the customer pays.
The lower bracket gives a fixed charge reduction of 0.10.
fix: Set discount = 0.90 before the final 1 - discount calculation.
Subtract 0.10 in cash instead of setting a rate.

diagnosis: The upper bracket needs 0.75 in the discount field.
The upper discount must be added to the subtotal as a surcharge.
The no-discount case should store 1 in discount.
Below the cutoff there is still a 10% discount.
Below the cutoff the customer should pay nothing.
fix: Return zero for the entire order in this branch.

diagnosis: The result should report the discount amount instead of the payable amount.
A percentage rate should be subtracted as a flat amount.
The checkout should round to two significant figures.
fix: Round the final charge to two significant figures.
